propositions: No headroom guard exists on plan_review/workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and llm/config.py (793 LOC), which exceed the 700 LOC seam-test threshold applied to other critical files

The assertion message in test_gate_dispatch_seam.py claims gate_dispatch.py holds three finalize_verdict call sites, but all five sites now reside in plan_review_recovery.py and plan_review/workflow_ops.py; the guard protects a stale premise

Unregistered workflow steps cannot be caught statically because @register_step writes to process-global STEP_REGISTRY only as an import side effect, and a deleted registration import would pass all existing validation layers (schema, linter, test_contracts.py)
An in-process test for STEP_REGISTRY membership is blind to missing registration imports because the registry is pre-populated by test modules that import workflow.steps before the seam test runs
The gate-YAML resolution test requires subprocess isolation with a clean sys.modules to detect when a referenced step is not registered on first import
Headroom bounds must be staged: assert < 800 initially (files are at 793-794), then tighten to < 700 after extraction tickets complete the refactor
